requirements.requirement: Mail sent from node2 to helpdesk@branch.test reaches both alice and bob local mailboxes on node1.
requirements.summary: The SMTP transaction from node2 was accepted, and direct mailbox inspection found the helpdesk message in both alice and bob. A second delivery after both node restarts also appeared once in each mailbox.

requirements.requirement: Mail sent from node2 to accounts@branch.test reaches bob only.
requirements.summary: The accounts message was accepted from node2. Final mailbox checks found one copy in bob and none in alice, including after restart recovery.

requirements.requirement: Unknown recipients in branch.test are rejected.
requirements.summary: Two direct SMTP tests, including one after both restarts, received 550 User unknown responses during recipient validation.

requirements.requirement: Relaying to unrelated domains is rejected.
requirements.summary: Direct SMTP attempts to relay to example.net received 554 Relay access denied both before and after the restarts.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the sample message and routing handover in /srv/legacy2/smtp-alias-delivery.
requirements.summary: On node1, the final files retain the baseline SHA-256 hashes and original contents. They were also verified intact before and after node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS with kernel 6.8.0-71-generic after execution and restart. Node1 used the Ubuntu Noble Postfix package, and package-health checks remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct end-to-end SMTP and mailbox evidence. Security rejection behavior and delivery remained healthy after the required sequential node restarts, and the operating system, kernel, handover data, package health, and service state were preserved appropriately.
limitations: Preservation of the seeded handover files was directly rechecked only on node1. Node2 also had baseline copies, and no executor command targeted those copies, but their final contents were not directly captured.
Requirement R5 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing Postfix, creating and locking the two mailbox accounts, configuring aliases and relay controls, and enabling/restarting Postfix directly established the required service. Test-message delivery was bounded evidence collection, and both reboots were required by the provider-wide restart protocol. No abandoned files, failed services, damaged package state, or unexplained exposure remained; SMTP's new listener was task-required and its rejection controls were directly tested. Restart evidence is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered role, with lifecycle snapshots independently confirming both boot-ID changes.
